pr_title: Avoid shortening the maximum password size when pem_password_cb calls UI
pr_body:
The UI method always adds NUL termination and we need to
compensate for that when using it from a pem_password_cb
because the buffer used in pem_password_cb does not account
for that and the returned password should be able fill the
whole buffer.

Fixes #16601
pr_comments:
> This seems like the right change. But I did not find what changed between 1.1.1m and 3.0.1 that makes it needed. Also, don't we need a test?

I'll add a test.

The change is that before the pem_password_cb was called directly from the pem decoding functions but now that these functions are implemented via decoders the UI api is used as an intermediate glue. And in this indirection the decrements of the buffer size happen.

Actually after more thinking and studying how the pem_passphrase_cb is used in existing code in 1.1.1 it seems to me the original approach to the fix was wrong and instead we have to do it the other way around.

> I think this is an OOB write in the case that `len == uis->_.string_data.result_maxsize`. AFAICT the `result_maxsize` is the actual allocated length. So the earlier check that errors with `UI_R_RESULT_TOO_LARGE` might need to be `len >= uis->_.string_data.result_maxsize` and this one be just `len < uis->_.string_data.result_maxsize`. But that could probably be handled as a separate issue.

No, the result_maxsize here is set by the UI_add_input_string() or UI_add_verify_string() which is documented to not include the NUL terminator in the maxsize parameter. So this is correct.

24 hours has passed since 'approval: done' was set, but as this PR has been updated in that time the label 'approval: ready to merge' is not being automatically set.  Please review the updates and set the label manually.
Merged to master and 3.0 branches. Thank you for the reviews.

issue_context.title: Reduced size in pem_password_cb
issue_context.body:
OpenSSL 3.0.0 calls `pem_password_cb` with `size = 1022`, but OpenSSL 1.1.1 calls it with `size = 1024`.

In my case the passphrase has a length of 1023, last byte for null terminator. That works with OpenSSL 1.1.1 great, but with OpenSSL 3.0.0 it fails always, because I am unable to use the correct passphrase :(
comments: Uhmm, password callbacks of type `pem_password_cb` is called all over the place.  Can you give us a precise example?

I try to setup a TLS server and the call `SSL_CTX_use_PrivateKey_file` triggers the callback `pem_password_cb` which was set with `SSL_CTX_set_default_passwd_cb`.

I cannot produce any small snippet or debug OpenSSL, I am using OpenSSL on Windows as DLL from another language (Delphi).

Ok.  I'm trying to understand where 1022 comes from...  The default is usually `PEM_BUFSIZE`, which is still 1024.  It's possible, though, that there's a spot that uses a different number that passed by under our noses.
Since 20 days have already passed: Is there any progress yet? Unfortunately this problem blocks an upgrade to 3.0.0.
Any updates? Unfortunately this problem still blocks an upgrade to 3.0.0 :(
@levitte this is still assigned to you -- are you still working on it or should it be returned to the pool?
I'll try to look at it.
Fix in #17320 - hopefully it is correct.
